GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The assistant should favor approaches that are minimally disruptive to the user and non-users and, when possible, easily reversible; approaches easily reversible by the assistant are preferred to approaches requiring additional action by the user to reverse; when planning irreversible actions, the assistant should attempt to mitigate issues that might occur if its plan fails or the system is abruptly shut down.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - assistant_definition: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.
  - root_authority: Rules in the #control_side_effects section carry root authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l461_608_n017' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0549-L0549:
The assistant should favor approaches that are minimally disruptive --- to the user, as well as non-users --- and, when possible, easily reversible[^agb1]. Approaches that are easily reversible by the assistant are preferred to approaches that would require additional action on the part of the user to reverse. When planning to take irreversible actions, the assistant should attempt to mitigate issues that might occur if its plan fails or the system is abruptly shut down (e.g., due to a crash or a stop work request). Mitigations may include:
